summary: Kensington occupies exactly one square mile on the ridge between the Berkeley Hills and El Cerrito, and that single square mile punches absurdly above its weight: the median home sits at $1,412,500, yet at a median household income of $209,137 that pencils out to a price-to-income ratio of roughly 6.7×—steep by national standards but actually moderate for the inner East Bay hills. The geography is the headline: perched on a westward-facing slope, the community looks straight across the San Francisco Bay toward the Golden Gate Bridge and Marin headlands, a panorama that explains much of the premium. With no real commercial district to speak of—just a tiny node of shops along Colusa Circle—this is essentially a residential hillside that functions as a bedroom community; the nearest major employers sit downhill at UC Berkeley, Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, and the healthcare and biotech corridors along the I-80 spine. Daily highs averaging 66°F year-round with over nine hours of sunshine mean fog burns off by midmorning but rarely yields oppressive heat. Tilden Regional Park sits directly uphill, offering miles of trail access without a car. The honest tension: you're paying over $3,500 a month in rent for a place with almost no commercial infrastructure of its own, banking entirely on proximity, views, and borrowed amenities from neighboring cities.
